text:
alex: quick heads-up — staging showed some odd notify ordering when multiplexing tenants onto the same pool. high-priority SLOs ended up queued behind lower-priority notify buckets.
mira: ugh, that's bad. can you paste the sequence that hit it?
alex: repro steps:
1) two tenants A (p99 latency SLO, notify=T1) and B (p95, notify=T2)
2) pool surge causes routing fallback to shared-capacity path
3) our notify dequeue used FIFO across pool instead of per-tenant priority, so T2 alerts went out before T1

sam: sounds like we treat notifications as a single global queue per pool. we discussed per-tenant priority before — did that never land?
jen: I thought we had a per-tenant priority flag in the routing policy, but maybe only used for compute allocation, not notify ordering.

alex: exact. compute routing honors priority but the notify pipeline flattens into a worker pool with no priority preservation. result: critical alerts delayed.

mira: ok. two axes: (A) preserve priority across the notify pipeline, (B) expose policy in console so tenant owners can preview ordering/impact.

sam: implementation-wise we can either (1) add priority queues per pool + weighted dequeue, or (2) tag notifications with (tenant, priority) and do a two-stage scheduler that prefers higher-priority tenants. (1) is heavier but simpler to reason about.

jen: for console UX — we need a preview that shows predicted notify latency under load. PMs want a "what-if" slider (burst size) and a visual queue ordering. Otherwise customers will be surprised by silent delays.

alex: rough config example i sketched:
```
notify_policy:
  preserve_priority: true
  dequeue_strategy: "per-tenant-priority" # options: fifo, per-tenant-priority, weighted
  backfill: true # allow lower tiers to use leftover capacity
  max_concurrent_notifications: 200
```

mira: love the preview idea. Also we should surface a telemetry metric: notify_queue_priority_fraction and notify_order_violations_count so we can catch regressions post-rollout.

sam: question: should this be tenant-configurable? i.e., let a tenant opt into strict priority (which might starve lower tiers) vs soft-priority (weighted)? exposing that in console feels advanced.

jen: product opinion: default soft-priority with a warning. advanced toggle for strict priority behind a feature flag and legal review (some customers will want guaranteed ordering for regulatory alerts).

alex: operational concern: strict priority could cause starvation in multi-tenant pools; we need safeguards (fairness windows, quota breaks) and tenancy-level circuit breaker.

mira: agree. propose: default route = soft-priority with a fairness window of 5s and a per-tenant min-throughput. show this in the preview and allow dry-run mode where console simulates behavior for a selected workload.

sam: API debate: do we add notify_priority to our /routes API (and model) or keep it only in console as a UX shim? other teams will want it in infra-as-code.

alex: want it in the API. Console can be a front-end, but infra-as-code + CLI needs the capability. we should version it: notify_priority v1 with clear semantics.

jen: UX followups: (1) Add a "Preview under load" button that runs a quick simulation using historical telemetry. (2) Surface clear copy: "Strict priority can delay lower-priority notify bundles." (3) Add an in-console dry-run toggle that writes no external notifs but records what would have been sent.

mira: dev plan: sam/infra to prototype the scheduler change (priority-preserving dequeue). alex to add telemetry hooks. jen to spec console preview / copy. I'll own rollout plan + canary metrics.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: branch=notify-priority-prototype, env=staging, owners=[sam, alex], ETA=2h

sam: i'll pick this up after current sprint item. quick first pass: per-pool priority buckets + weighted round robin with preemption.

alex: thanks. can we add an alert for notify_order_violations_count > 0 in staging so we don't merge without catching it?

mira: yes — add a gating SLO: notify-ordering-regression = count==0 over 1h for staging. if it trips, block rollout.

jen: noted. i'll add a console note to the SLO editor that sets expectations about notify ordering for shared pools.

alex: cool. meeting? 15 min sync after lunch to align APIs/telemetry.

mira: +1. ping me 12:30 :spiral_calendar:

sam: i'll be there :thumbsup:

jen: thanks all :bell:
